findings.title: 5 Defendants Charged Federally with Running Scheme that Targeted Victim Companies via Phishing Text Messages
findings.summary_md: The US Attorney's Office for the Central District of California announced charges against five defendants accused of running a scheme that targeted victim companies through phishing text messages. The release says a criminal complaint unsealed that day charged Tyler Robert Buchanan, 22, of the United Kingdom with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy, wire fraud, and aggravated identity theft. The page is dated Wednesday, November 20, 2024, almost two years before the sentencing coverage in this story.

findings.title: US charges five in 'Scattered Spider' hacking scheme
findings.summary_md: Reuters reported on November 20, 2024 that US prosecutors had charged five people in a hacking scheme linked to Scattered Spider. The report was filed at 22:34 UTC by Jonathan Stempel and A.J. Vicens. It is the earliest mainstream news item located for the five-defendant case that ended with Buchanan's sentencing.

findings.title: Alleged Scattered Spider SIM-swapper must pay back $13.2M to 59 victims
findings.summary_md: The Register reported that Noah Michael Urban, a co-defendant in the California case, pleaded guilty to wire fraud and aggravated identity theft charges and agreed to pay over $13.2 million in restitution to 59 victims. The offenses covered August 2022 to March 2023, and the article names Elbadawy, Osiebo, Evans and Tyler Robert Buchanan as the other defendants in the same indictment. Investigators found victim passwords, wallet credentials and transaction histories on Urban's computer, along with browser history showing logins to victim email accounts.

findings.title: British man pleads guilty to conspiring to steal $8m in virtual currency
findings.summary_md: The BBC reported that Tyler Buchanan, 24, of Dundee pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of aggravated identity theft. The report says he and co-conspirators used SMS phishing against at least a dozen companies and stole at least $8 million from people in the United States between September 2021 and April 2023. A device found at his home in Scotland held names and addresses of victims, cryptocurrency seed phrases and login details for one victim account. Sentencing was then scheduled for August 21 with a 22-year statutory maximum.

findings.title: Scot becomes second Scattered Spider-linked crook to plead guilty in US
findings.summary_md: The Register reported that Buchanan pleaded guilty in California and faced a statutory maximum of 22 years, with sentencing then set for August 21, 2026. It describes aliases including Dread Pirate Roberts, Evefan and tylerb, and phishing lures warning that a VPN was about to expire. The article says the defendants paid for domains and copycat websites, and that April 2023 evidence at Buchanan's Scottish residence included a text file of wallet seed phrases and one victim's login details.
